# DropSpace 1.1 Beta1 — Retrieve, collect, reference and listen

<!-- update-summary: Adds unified Island retrieval, opt-in recent-file collection, reusable processing results, a shared reference window, local Agent access, and an independent music window with responsive lyrics and Windows volume control. -->

- Find clipboard history, Temporary Space, pinned items, recent files and processing results from the existing global shortcut and Island search. Copy text or file objects, drag files out, or choose the explicitly labeled copy-path action.
- Enable file relay for folders you choose. DropSpace watches new files in each selected folder's top level, waits until they are readable and stable, and filters temporary downloads and internal resources. It does not scan your disk or import existing files. Recent records support preview, retain and removal without deleting their external originals.
- Reuse successful ZIP, image conversion/resizing and ordinary download results directly from the Island. Results remain searchable after the processing view closes; watched-file and task-result records merge by path. Failed, cancelled and intermediate outputs are excluded.
- Open images or plain text in one movable, resizable reference window. It shares the original content record, supports image zoom and long-text scrolling, and stays available when the Island closes. Closing the window only ends viewing.
- Connect local Agents through a discoverable catalog of 136 commands, a PowerShell client or an optional MCP bridge. Pair once using a random key, then use the saved credential; revoke access from DropSpace settings. The copyable Skill installation prompt works independently of the selected interface language.
- Open a separate music window that shares the app's playback session, lyrics, translations and timeline. Responsive cover and lyrics layouts animate between states, portrait lyric controls fade after inactivity, and the volume slider controls Windows system volume. Lyrics and translation icons share an evenly spaced row below the volume bar. An optional global shortcut opens the same window.
- Refine shared action icons, align the Island search and close controls across its pages, and enforce a usable minimum main-window size with DPI and work-area adjustments.

Background file arrivals and processing completion do not open the Island, take focus or switch away from music. Existing output locations and originals are retained. v1.0.0 is the immediate upgrade baseline for this release.

## Downloads and requirements

Windows 11 x64 or Windows Server 2022 x64 (build 20348 or later). Choose `DropSpaceSetup.exe` for installation, `DropSpace.exe` for Portable, or the MSIX package for Windows-managed deployment. Portable updates use manual replacement. Optional AI models and the independent CUDA component retain their existing bytes; this release does not claim new model-quality validation.

## Beta validation and limits

Focused checks covered the four content workflows, local Agent pairing and revocation, native window lifecycle, system-volume writes and restoration, shortcuts, transition intermediate frames and three final control layouts. A separate real Windows media-session probe verified pause, resume and seek through the shared media service. Most presentation checks used synthetic media data; they do not establish compatibility with every third-party player or validate audible process-loopback capture.

The final music icon/layout pixel review and updated screenshots remain incomplete because the desktop-control tool remained in a stopped state. Native geometry checks passed, but they are not a substitute for visual review. Long touch/inertial scrolling, the full DPI/language matrix, physical IME candidate interactions and complete third-party OLE drag-and-drop were not comprehensively exercised.

Agent access is local to this Windows user. Cloud Agents need a local executor; the optional MCP bridge requires Node.js 18 or later. Authorization management, account secrets and arbitrary shell execution are not exposed as app commands. Existing Windows permission and confirmation flows still apply. Folder relay cannot guarantee recovery of every event during folder outages or watcher overflow; external originals are preserved.
